classification.difficultyReason: Identify cancellation of opposite ordinates on two unscaled curves, including a tangential intercept.

content.prompt: Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ below, estimate where the $x$-intercepts of $y=f(x)+g(x)$ are.

spec.description: Wide unscaled coordinate sketch with positive-direction axis arrows, x and y labels, one blue oscillation and two red oscillations. No ticks, grid, origin label, curve labels or curve endpoint arrows.
spec.mathematics: Editable schematic Bézier reconstruction of the supplied curves. Drawing coordinates are internal layout units, not numerical source values or asserted function equations. Preserve equal and opposite ordinates beneath the blue maximum and at two locations surrounding its minimum.
spec.answerVisibility: Component curves only; no intercept markers or summed curve.

answer.worked: At an $x$-intercept, $f(x)+g(x)=0$. The two ordinates must be equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. This occurs beneath the blue curve’s positive maximum and at two positions on either side of its negative minimum, as marked.

spec.sourceRegion: Concept Check question 8; answer positions from teacher PDF page 5
spec.description: Complete component-curve sketch with three purple markers on the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: The markers identify cancellation beneath the blue positive maximum and on both sides of its negative minimum. No numerical x-coordinates are claimed. The first intercept need not cross the axis.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer markers appear only in the solution figure.
